message.content:
**Answer**

The last common ancestor of a lion (*Panthera leo*) and a zebra (*Equus zebra*) is the last common ancestor of all **placental mammals** (Eutheria).  
- Lions belong to the order **Carnivora** (family Felidae).  
- Zebras belong to the order **Perissodactyla** (family Equidae).  

The two orders diverged from each other deep in the mammalian tree, so their most recent shared ancestor is a small, insect‑eating mammal that lived roughly **160–200 million years ago** during the late Jurassic–early Cretaceous period. This ancestor would have been a member of the clade that eventually gave rise to all modern placental mammals.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want the common ancestor of lion and zebra. Lion is a big cat (Panthera leo), zebra is a horse family (Equus zebra). Both are mammals, but more specifically both are in the order Carnivora (lion) and Perissodactyla (zebra). They share a common ancestor at the level of mammals, maybe at the level of placental mammals. The common ancestor would be a mammal from the Eutheria clade. The earliest common ancestor of all placental mammals is the last common ancestor of all eutherians, which lived around 160-200 million years ago. But maybe they want the common ancestor of the two species: the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae. That would be a common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all modern mammals except monotremes and marsupials. That would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals, which is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That ancestor would be a small mammal from the Paleocene or earlier. So answer: the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, likely a small, insectivorous mammal that lived around 160-200 million years ago. Or we can say: the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals. So answer accordingly.
